epoch_gate_pilot: results/female_finetune/pilot_epoch_gate.json (fold0 cnn1d seed42: epochs=2 delta=+0.149 [CI non-overlapping], epochs=3 delta=+0.148 -- no added benefit, 2 epochs locked)
bounded_claim: Fine-tuning shows what the model CAN RECRUIT to help with a new group, not what the original model was USING. This is true for both conditions.
male_control_asymmetry: The male-control pool is NOT a clean analogue of the female pool, in TWO confounded ways: (1) exposure -- the 10 val-only males had zero gradient updates but DID influence checkpoint selection (weak exposure, not true zero exposure like the 12 women); (2) ceiling -- the male-only model's pre-fine-tune accuracy on these males is already very high (0.92-0.99, vs 0.79-0.93 for the women), leaving far less headroom for fine-tuning to show ANY improvement regardless of mechanism. Both confounds bias the male-control condition toward showing a SMALLER delta than the female condition even under a purely generic-adaptation story. Therefore: if female and male-control signatures MATCH (layer-change / band-shift analyses), that is STRONG evidence for generic adaptation (agreement despite two biases pushing toward disagreement). If they DIFFER, that CANNOT be reported as a clean female-specific finding -- it is confounded with novel-vs-familiar exposure AND with ceiling/headroom, not sex alone. Report differences as 'suggestive, control-confounded', never as a clean female-specific claim.
n_flag_female: fine-tune female n<=9, eval female n=3 per fold -- within-sample, not a population claim
n_flag_male_control: male-control fine-tune n<=8, eval n<=3 per fold, drawn from val-only (weak-exposure) males -- within-sample, control-confounded, not a clean zero-exposure analogue
pooling_note: Fold spread is reported (min/max of the seed-averaged per-fold delta); folds are NEVER pooled into one tighter CI across folds (locked out-of-scope decision).
pre_registered_gate: If female fine-tuning doesn't reliably improve female accuracy, the 'what changed' analysis has nothing to localize -- flag as null. If it does improve, compare magnitude to male-control: comparable -> generic adaptation at the behavioral level; larger -> proceed to the layer-change / band-shift analyses but do NOT claim female-specificity from accuracy alone, since the male-control asymmetry above predicts a smaller male-control delta even under pure generic adaptation.

cnn1d.text: Female fine-tuning helps substantially more than the male-control condition at the behavioral level, BUT this asymmetry is expected even under generic adaptation because of the exposure and ceiling confounds (see male_control_asymmetry note) -- this alone does NOT establish a female-specific mechanism. Proceed to the layer-change / band-shift analyses (frequency/layer double-difference) to determine whether the mechanism is genuinely different, reporting any such finding as suggestive and control-confounded, never clean.
